the cause, measured, and how I fix it

I told you this was working, and it was not. I tested it with a routine I had just created — and that is the one shape where the bug cannot appear. You pushed back twice before I looked properly. Everything below is measured on your build.

NOTHING WAS EVER BEING COPIED. One chip was quietly holding two occurrences of the same routine. Moving it moved one of them, and the other — which had been there all along, hidden underneath — became visible.

last week’s one, which you postponed to today  ┐
                                       ├─ ONE chip on 17 Nov
today’s own one, due anyway              ┘

you drag that chip to 18 Nov
  → one of the two goes
  → the other is still on 17 Nov — and looks like a copy

Measured on your build: occurrences scheduled on 17 Nov, before any drag: 1 — one chip, two records underneath it.

Why my first fix did not help. I shipped one on 17 Nov that corrected a real fault, but every routine I tested with had never been dragged before. Yours have been dragged for days. A routine with no move history cannot show this at all, which is why I kept reporting it fixed while you kept seeing it broken.

THE FIX — you chose this. When a postponed occurrence lands on a day the routine is already due, they become one. Postponing it moves the whole thing, and you never see two. (A, 2026-11-17, from three options.)

It is fixed in one place that every way of moving a date goes through, so the tree date chip, Today/Tomorrow, the month grid, the week grid and the day grid are all covered without touching eleven separate pieces of code.

One attempt was built and thrown away. It wrote a marker for each hop. Dragging the same chip seven days running showed it corrupting the stored data — four chips after six moves — so it never reached you. The shipped version keeps one record per occurrence instead, and the stored data stays the same size however often you drag.

What is NOT changed: the routine itself never moves. Its schedule, its start date and every future occurrence stay exactly where they were — that is what you chose when I asked (move only the one I dragged), and the roll-over you rely on (keep it as it is) is untouched.

I ALSO THOUGHT OF — three things your request does not decide.

  • The duplicates already sitting in your planner. This stops new ones appearing; it does not tidy the ones that are there. Each clears itself the next time you drag it. I can sweep them all at once instead — but that edits your stored data, so I will not do it unless you say so. Say “sweep the old ones”.
  • The spare copy on screen is clickable. If you tick the one on the wrong day, the planner records that day as done. Dragging is safe; ticking is the one that writes something you may not mean.
  • Merging hides that you missed one. That is the trade you chose: last week’s outstanding one and this week’s become a single chip, so the calendar stays clean but it no longer shows that you are a week behind. If you ever want that visible — a count on the chip, or a mark — that is a separate card, not a change to this one.
